candidate.title: Reliability of crop-disease AI under field-domain shift and data contamination
candidate.workingTitle: Evaluating the Impact of Dataset Contamination and Field-Domain Shift on the Reliability of AI-Based Crop-Disease Recognition
candidate.summary: Can crop-disease AI retain calibrated confidence and useful selective prediction under leakage-resistant evaluation and cross-domain field shift, especially when tested on Ghanaian field imagery?
candidate.shortDescription: A reproducible evaluation of leakage-aware splits, field-domain shift, calibration, and selective prediction, with Ghanaian field relevance where feasible.
candidate.ghanaianRelevance: Field agriculture in Ghana is a possible setting, not a requirement. Public datasets are preferred unless local images can be collected properly.
candidate.technicalContribution: A leakage-resistant, cross-domain reliability evaluation for crop-disease recognition, with particular attention to calibration and selective prediction. A few-shot vision-language model (VLM) comparison is a candidate component, not the thesis contribution by itself.

feasibility.rationale: This is a planning assessment. The work is measurable if a public dataset's provenance and split metadata can be audited.

candidate.dataRequirements: Candidate leads discussed include CCMT (reported in project notes as 24,881 original images plus 102,976 augmented images, four crops and 22 categories), PlantVillage, Cassava, Pear, PlantDoc, AgriPath-LF16 (reported lead: 111,000 images, 16 crops, 41 diseases), and a 360-image wheat field set discussed with BLAP. These counts and dataset details are unverified; check versions, licensing, source/plant/session IDs, duplicates, augmentation provenance, and field conditions before selection.
candidate.evaluationDesign: Prioritise original-image provenance and leakage-resistant grouping. Never treat augmented copies as independent observations. Compare random image splits with source/session/farm/plant-disjoint splits where identifiers support them. Evaluate cross-domain transfer and confidence calibration/selective prediction, not accuracy alone. Candidate metrics discussed include macro-F1, class recall, robustness/degradation gap, calibration, risk-coverage, and inference cost. If a VLM is included, use the same split and shift protocol as conventional baselines.
majorRisks: The candidate datasets may not expose source, plant, session, location, or duplicate metadata needed to test leakage rigorously.
The proposed public datasets may differ in crops, disease labels, image conditions, and licences; they cannot be combined casually.
The recent literature leads (Ye, Xiong/BLAP, Kang, AgriPath-LF16) have not been fully bibliographically and methodologically verified.
Adding few-shot vision-language models, Ghanaian field collection, explainability, and multiple crops at once would make the study too broad.
openDecisions: Which dataset has sufficient provenance and a defensible leakage-resistant split?
Does CCMT expose original-image relationships and source/session metadata, or can related images be identified robustly?
Should the primary framing be few-shot VLM reliability under cross-domain shift, or a model-agnostic reliability protocol?
Can Ghanaian field imagery be obtained with labels and provenance, or should public cross-domain datasets be the sole experimental basis?

nodes.title: Curated crop-disease accuracy may not be reliable in the field
nodes.summary: A strong score on a cleaned image set can hide leakage, poor calibration, and a drop when the photographs come from real fields.
nodes.detail: The project discussions rejected another generic crop-disease classifier as a weak contribution. The sharper problem is that high scores on curated datasets may overstate real-world reliability if correlated images or leakage cross the train/test boundary, and if field conditions differ from the benchmark. The thesis should test these mechanisms with a reproducible protocol rather than claim that all existing scores are inflated. A specific dataset concern discussed was that CCMT reportedly contains 24,881 original images and 102,976 augmented images across four crops and 22 categories, with identical/augmented train-test overlap reported in prior notes. These figures and the overlap claim are not independently verified in this data package.
assumptions: A public dataset exists with enough provenance or image similarity structure to test a meaningful split strategy.
Reliability should be evaluated beyond top-line accuracy.
risks: If the dataset does not permit a defensible leakage audit, the contamination component must be narrowed or dropped.

nodes.title: How well do crop-disease models maintain predictive confidence calibration and selective prediction under leakage-resistant cross-domain evaluation?
nodes.summary: How do dataset contamination and field-domain shift affect predictive reliability, confidence calibration, and selective prediction?
nodes.detail: The primary question concerns the effect of leakage/correlated sampling and field-domain shift on model performance, confidence calibration, and selective prediction. A discussion explored few-shot vision-language models on Ghanaian field imagery, but the study should not become a broad model comparison. The evaluation protocol is the core contribution. A narrower candidate framing discussed on 16 November was few-shot VLM crop-disease recognition under cross-domain shift, particularly Ghanaian field imagery. It remains a candidate framing, not a confirmed research gap.

nodes.title: Why reliability is the contribution
nodes.summary: The field already has many classifiers. The opening is in how performance is measured.
nodes.detail: The study is relevant to Ghanaian agriculture because model performance in deployment depends on real field conditions, not only curated benchmarks. Ghana-specific images would strengthen contextual relevance but are not mandatory if public datasets support a rigorous experiment. The computing contribution is reliability evaluation for computer-vision systems.

nodes.title: Local field images are optional
nodes.summary: Local field images are optional
nodes.detail: Public datasets are the default. Ghana-specific field photographs may be added only if collection and annotation are feasible. They are not required to state the problem.

nodes.summary: An evaluation protocol for vision models
nodes.detail: The technical contribution is experimental design and evaluation: data-provenance audit, leakage-aware partitioning, domain-shift construction, calibration analysis, and selective prediction. It is not simply training a new crop classifier.

nodes.summary: What would count as a contribution
nodes.detail: A reproducible protocol and empirical evidence showing how split strategy and field shift change both predictive performance and trustworthiness. The thesis should report uncertainty and coverage-risk trade-offs rather than a single accuracy score.

nodes.title: High curated accuracy is a weak deployment claim
nodes.summary: High curated accuracy is a weak deployment claim
nodes.detail: The discussions noted that crop-disease recognition is already a crowded classification area. PlantVillage, Cassava, Pear, and PlantDoc were mentioned in connection with a Description-Guided CLIP lead (Ye et al., 2026); BLAP (Xiong et al., 2026) was discussed in connection with OOD, leave-one-crop-out, severity, and recommendation validation. These are literature leads, not verified summaries. One reported limitation was that conventional confidence calibration was not clearly covered in the notes; this must be checked in the full texts. A reported CCMT description in project notes gives 24,881 original images plus 102,976 augmented images, four crops and 22 categories, and raises concern about identical/augmented overlap across splits. Treat this as an audit lead: confirm the dataset release, counts, metadata, and actual split construction before making any claim.

nodes.title: Reported test scores may not survive a change of field conditions
nodes.summary: Reported test scores may not survive a change of field conditions
nodes.detail: The proposed gap is not simply that field images are harder. It is whether reported predictive reliability survives documented changes in acquisition conditions and data source, and whether confidence remains meaningful under those shifts. Ye et al. and AgriPath-LF16 were noted as relevant leads, but exact datasets, split protocols, and field conditions have not been verified. The more specific unresolved question raised in the discussion is whether leakage-resistant evaluation changes confidence calibration, uncertainty, and selective prediction—not merely accuracy—under external/field domain shift.
risks: Do not expand this into explainability, fairness, compression, and diagnosis at once.
validationRequirements: Extract the exact datasets, crops, disease classes, split strategy, and acquisition conditions from each paper.
Identify whether the test set is genuinely external/field-based or merely a different curated dataset.
Avoid claiming a gap if a directly comparable evaluation already exists.

nodes.summary: Leakage and correlated splits
nodes.detail: Near-duplicate images, capture sessions, or the same plant appearing on both sides of a split.

nodes.title: Random image splits can leak near-duplicates
nodes.summary: Random image splits can leak near-duplicates
nodes.detail: The discussions raised the risk that random image-level splits can place near-duplicates, images from the same plant, or images from the same capture session in both training and test sets. Kang (2026) was mentioned as a lead on leakage/session-aware splits, and CCMT as a possible dataset with a reported 24,881 original images. Neither the citation details nor dataset count/provenance are verified. The notes also mention a Kang (2026) lead reporting that 91.9% of CDD test images share sensor readings with training images. The exact study, dataset, and meaning of sensor-reading overlap are unverified; the methodological implication to investigate is session/farm-disjoint evaluation.
risks: The proposed leakage analysis depends on actual duplicate/capture metadata or a defensible similarity-based audit.

nodes.title: Random splits may overstate generalisation when images are correlated
nodes.summary: Random splits may overstate generalisation when images are correlated
nodes.detail: A candidate gap is that random image-level splits may overestimate generalisation when images are correlated by plant, session, source, or near-duplicate content. This must be tested against the selected dataset documentation and literature; do not assume a random split is contaminated without evidence. A key rule from the discussions: split original images first and keep augmented versions of an original in the same partition. Augmented copies must never be counted as independent test observations.
validationRequirements: Audit near-duplicates and source/session grouping before selecting split methods.
Report the unit of grouping and justify why it blocks the relevant leakage path.

nodes.detail: Whether accuracy hides overconfident or poorly calibrated predictions when the field distribution changes.

nodes.title: Accuracy does not describe confidence
nodes.summary: Accuracy does not describe confidence
nodes.detail: The project discussions distinguished accuracy from confidence quality. A model can retain reasonable accuracy while being poorly calibrated or confidently wrong under domain shift. BLAP (Xiong et al., 2026) was noted as a lead touching OOD and related evaluation dimensions; the exact calibration measures in that work are unverified. The discussions specifically identified the distinction between local evidence calibration and conventional predictive-confidence calibration. Ye et al. (2026) was reported to use Description-Guided CLIP with 16-shot accuracies of 93.16% (PlantVillage), 79.30% (Cassava), and 96.56% (Pear), and 56.96% on 21-class PlantDoc cross-domain evaluation. These are unverified project notes and must be checked against the paper.

nodes.title: Accuracy can hide unsafe confidence under distribution shift
nodes.summary: Accuracy can hide unsafe confidence under distribution shift
nodes.detail: The candidate gap is the joint evaluation of predictive performance, calibration, and selective prediction under the same documented contamination and field-shift conditions. Whether recent systems already cover this combination remains to be established from full-text review. The proposed focus is whether a model’s confidence is calibrated and whether selective prediction can reduce high-confidence errors while retaining useful coverage under domain shift. Do not infer conventional confidence calibration from local evidence calibration.
validationRequirements: Select calibration metrics appropriate to the task and report their limitations.
Compare risk/coverage curves or another justified selective-prediction evaluation.

nodes.title: Another classifier bake-off is not the contribution
nodes.summary: Another classifier bake-off is not the contribution
nodes.detail: The discussions considered few-shot vision-language models and a possible Ghanaian field-image evaluation. The working idea was to compare conventional models with a selected VLM under a fixed leakage-aware protocol. This is optional: a model-family comparison should be included only if it clarifies the reliability question and does not turn the thesis into a broad benchmark. The VLM direction was motivated by the Description-Guided CLIP lead and BLAP. Project notes describe BLAP as 990 images across 11 crops and 33 categories, reporting 92.78% accuracy, plus a 360-image wheat-field set with 36/36 test images reportedly correct. Exact details and evaluation conditions are unverified.

nodes.title: It is unknown whether vision-language models change the failure mode
nodes.summary: It is unknown whether vision-language models change the failure mode
nodes.detail: A possible question is whether a selected few-shot vision-language approach changes the pattern of failure, calibration, or selective prediction under the same field shift. This is not yet a confirmed literature gap and may be removed if it expands the study beyond a one-year MPhil. The potential novelty is not simply using a VLM. It is evaluating whether few-shot VLMs maintain calibration and useful selective prediction under cross-domain field shift when the split protocol blocks leakage. Include the VLM only if literature review confirms this question is not already answered and the experiment remains bounded.
validationRequirements: Establish a specific reason to include a VLM from the literature, not novelty-by-model choice.
Use the same data, shift conditions, and evaluation protocol for all compared model families.
